title: Gaspar Aguilar & San Vicente Mártir Get New Bike Lanes
text:
Valencia is making significant strides in improving its urban landscape for cyclists! this article dives into the city’s enterprising project too expand its cycling network, making Valencia even more bike-amiable. learn how this initiative is enhancing the city’s infrastructure with new bike lanes and what cyclists can expect from these exciting developments.
Valencia Expands Cycling network with New Bike Lanes Project Highlights The project will add approximately 3,100 meters of cycling network to the southern neighborhoods of Valencia, including Arrapins, Patraix , Favara, La Raïosa, Creu Cuerta, and Sant Marcel·lí. The initiative, originating from the 2017 Decideim VLC Budgets, is 90% funded by European Next Generation funds . Overview of the “Road Reorganization” Project Valencia is set to enhance its cycling infrastructure through the “Road Reorganization of Gaspar Aguilar Avenue and San Vicente Street” project. This initiative, stemming from the participatory budgets of Decoimvlc 2017, encompasses four key actions designed to improve connectivity and accessibility for cyclists across the city.
The project includes:
Construction of a bike lane and road reorganization on Gaspar Aguilar Avenue. Construction of a bike lane and road reorganization on San Vicente Mártir Street. A new bike lane along Dr. Tomás sala service road, connecting San Vicente Mártir with Pío IX. A new bike lane on Joaquín Navarro Street . Gaspar Aguilar avenue: A 1,200-Meter Cycling Itinerary The cycling route on Gaspar Aguilar Avenue will span 1,200 meters, running from Jesús Plaza to Doctor Tomás sala. This route will connect with existing bike lanes on Jesús Street, jeroni Munyós-Beat Nicolau Factor, Ranes Llanera, and Tres Creus-Doctor tomás Sala. the bidirectional bike lane will be segregated from the road, situated between the east sidewalk and a cord parking lane.
Along with the bike lane, the avenue will undergo a restructuring of circulation lanes. Two lanes will be maintained towards Dr. Tomás sala Avenue, while the direction towards Campos Crespo will be reduced to a single lane. This adjustment aims to provide more space for pedestrians, improve accessibility, and facilitate the installation of two new traffic light-controlled pedestrian crossings.
san Vicente Mártir Street: A 1,600-Meter addition The new bike lane on San vicente Mártir Street will extend 1,600 meters from the intersection with Mestre Sosa to Dr. Tomás Sala Avenue. It will connect with existing two-way bike lanes, as well as those on Giorgeta and Dolores Alcaide. This bidirectional bike lane will primarily run segregated on the road, adjacent to the west sidewalk.
Similar to Gaspar Aguilar Avenue, San Vicente Mártir Street will also see a restructuring of circulation lanes, with a single lane in the direction of Doctor Tomás Sala between Giorgeta and the south Boulevard.
Dr. Tomás Sala service Road: Connecting Key Points The project includes a bike lane along the service road of Avenida by Dr. Tomás Sala, connecting San Vicente Mártir with the Cultural Center of La Rambleta (C/ de Pío IX). In the section between San Vicente Mártir and La Rotonda de San Marcel·lí, a unidirectional bike lane will be established on the sidewalk, heading towards La Rambleta. This will complement the existing cyclocalle that runs along the service road towards San Vicente Mártir.the remaining portion of the route to Pius IX will feature a bidirectional bike lane, segregated on the road between the north sidewalk and the battery parking area.
Joaquín Navarro Street: A 300-Meter Link A 300-meter bike lane will be constructed on Joaquín Navarro Street,stretching from the intersection with Porteros Street to the connection with San Vicente Mártir. This new cycling route will be bidirectional and segregated from the road on the southern sidewalk.In the initial section, between Porteros and santiago suárez Square, parking will be arranged in a battery style, while the rest of the street towards San Vicente Mártir will offer cord-style parking.
Technical Specifications and Timeline The bike lanes will generally have a width of 2.30 to 2.50 meters, with narrower sections (1.70 meters) at bus stops to facilitate access to EMT (Municipal Transportation Company) stops. In certain areas, the bike lanes will be located on the sidewalk, including the intersection of Joaquín Navarro and Porteros, the crossing with Giorgeta, and the service road of Tomás Sala.
The project is estimated to take 12 months to complete, allowing for simultaneous work across diffrent areas. Individually, the estimated timelines for each area are:
Gaspar Aguilar: 7 months san Vicente Mártir: 5 months Dr.Tomás Sala service road: 2 months Joaquín Navarro: 2 months funding and Budget The project has a budget of €2,650,956.60, which includes €2,190,873.22 plus €460,083.38 for VAT (Value Added Tax). It has received significant financial support, with 90% of the base budget (excluding VAT) being funded through the European Next Generation funds.
This substantial investment underscores Valencia’s commitment to sustainable urban development and promoting cycling as a viable mode of transportation.
